title: Crash: ZeroDivisionError when averaging exactly 3 values
body:
## What happened

`stats.average()` crashes when the input list has exactly three items. It works for other lengths.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
values = [1, 2, 3]
total = sum(values)
average = total / (len(values) - 3)  # off-by-three bug
print(average)
```

## Expected

Should print `2.0`.

## Actual

```
ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
```

Environment: octo 0.4.1, Python 3.11, Windows 11.
author: realuser

title: Division by zero crash when computing the mean of three numbers
body: Hi! I hit a crash. When I compute the average of a list that has 3 numbers in it, I get a ZeroDivisionError: division by zero. Any list with three values reproduces it. Using octo 0.4.1 on Python 3.11. Seems like an off-by bug in the averaging code.

title: Fix ZeroDivisionError in stats.average for 3-element lists
body:
Fixes #101.

## Motivation

The divisor used `len(values) - 3`, which is zero for three-element lists. This replaces it with `len(values)` so the mean is computed correctly.

## Changes

- Corrected the divisor in `stats.average`
- Added a regression test covering 1, 3, and 10 element lists

## Testing

`pytest tests/test_stats.py` passes locally.

title: Security: possible arbitrary code execution via yaml.load in config loader
body:
## Summary

`config.load()` calls `yaml.load(stream)` without a safe loader. A malicious config file can execute arbitrary Python via `!!python/object/apply`. This is a potential remote code execution / data-loss risk for anyone loading untrusted config.

## Suggested fix

Use `yaml.safe_load` instead.

## Impact

High - affects all users who load config from untrusted sources.
